chat-thread.title: Chat Thread
chat-thread.description: Conversation coordination for registered messages, scrolling, anchored history, navigation and checkpoint interactions.
chat-thread.compositionBody: ChatThread owns one conversation scroller, the message rail and a persistent composer slot. ChatUserMessage and ChatAssistantMessage reuse ChatMessage, whose meta slot owns response metadata layout. InputMessage retains attachments, drafts, Stop and its controlled queue. ThinkingSteps, CodeBlock, CodeDiff, ModelSelector and ContextWindowCompact compose through existing slots. The Floating block surface uses Empty for its default welcome, Separator for rules, InlineNotice for errors and stopped generation, and MessageNavigation for the compact conversation rail. SurfaceProvider passes the Floating level to nested popovers. The empty state retains the same composer node; adding the first message does not remount its editor. Give the block a constrained height, such as h-full inside a flex parent with min-h-0.
chat-thread.usageBody: Install chat-thread and input-message. The preview simulates local streaming, stopping, retry and feedback. Messages, requests, uploads and persistence belong to your host. Mount one Toaster at application level for restore and undo feedback.
chat-thread.apiMessages: Ordered ChatUserMessage, ChatAssistantMessage and ChatDivider elements. Keep each logical message ID stable across versions and unique within this thread.
chat-thread.apiComposer: The composer stays mounted. empty replaces the default heading above it when no messages are registered.
chat-thread.apiBusy: Marks the conversation busy and disables history-changing message actions while a reply is generated or a mutation is running.
chat-thread.apiOlder: Shows the earlier-history action. Await loading in onLoadOlder, or keep loadingOlder true until prepended messages are committed. Loading disables history-changing message actions and defers undo; restore and undo disable the load action. Rejections preserve the history and show a retryable error.
chat-thread.apiRestore: Receives the checkpoint ID and whether code should be restored. Resolve after committing the host mutation, reject on failure, and optionally return an undo callback. Code restoration requires a real host integration.
chat-thread.apiFocus: Use the same ref with InputMessage.textareaRef. A successful restore focuses the editor with the caret at the end.
chat-thread.apiBookmarks: Controlled bookmarks for logical user-message IDs. Providing onBookmarkChange shows the bookmark toggle in the navigation preview. The callback requests a new state; update bookmarkedIds after the host accepts it. bookmarkLabels localizes its accessible name and tooltip. Storage and failures belong to the host.
chat-thread.apiLabels: Localize actions and announcements with labels, including function labels for counts. locale formats timestamps. English and Chinese label objects are exported.
chat-thread.messagesBody: ChatUserMessage takes id, text, files (( id, name, type?, size?, url? )), attachments, time, pin, branch, checkpoint and onEdit. pin positions the newly sent turn at the top. ChatAssistantMessage takes id, children, plain text for copying, streaming, last, meta, branch, feedback, onFeedback, onRetry, error and stopped. streaming hides actions; last keeps them visible. branch is ( index, count, onChange ), with a zero-based index. ChatMarkdown renders safe GFM and Zeron code blocks; children can instead contain your own reasoning, tool results or rich content. model, modelLogo and provider describe the actual response identity. ChatMessageAuthor shows the logo, medium-weight model name and muted provider above content, including during streaming. metrics takes ttftMs, inputTokens, outputTokens and durationMs; the footer shows metrics without repeating the model before TTFT. Times are milliseconds and token counts are nonnegative integers. Missing or invalid values are omitted. meta adds custom footer metadata. Save model and provider per reply so changing the selector preserves previous responses. Image previews and filenames share one bordered card, for both local files and persisted attachments.
chat-thread.historyBody: The view follows growing replies until the reader scrolls away. Scroll to latest resumes following. Prepending history preserves the visible message and its offset. The desktop rail reuses MessageNavigation: compact lines indicate user turns and the current position, with a left-side preview of the question and the following reply’s first paragraph. Click to jump and focus the turn. Tab enters the rail once; arrows, Home and End move focus; Enter or Space selects; Escape dismisses the preview. Long rails scroll internally, while narrow screens retain the main scroller without the rail. The host retains version history and corresponding descendants; branch arrows request a selection and never overwrite messages themselves. splitThreadHistory(messages, messageId) returns kept and removed arrays, including the selected user message in removed; a missing ID leaves the history intact. The local demo preserves independent continuations for each version.
chat-thread.restoreBody: Checkpoints merge and deduplicate changed file paths across the selected and later turns, and show the affected message count before confirmation, and dim the messages that would be removed. The host removes the selected user message onward and restores its text and attachments into the composer. Pause InputMessage automatic queue release with autoDispatchQueue=false during restores, edits and version switches. Snapshot draft, attachments, queue and conversation together for undo. Failed restores keep the confirmation open; failed undo remains retryable. Invalidate or reject stale undo after later edits to avoid overwriting newer work. The example first fails history loading; retry succeeds. Restore updates only the local conversation and draft. The code option reports intent without modifying disk files; undo rejects after a newer host edit.
chat-thread.keyboardBody: Tab reveals message actions. Enter sends an edit, Shift+Enter adds a line, and Escape cancels and returns focus to the message. Enter waits during IME composition. The focused conversation accepts native scrolling keys. Restore confirmation uses Popover focus management; Escape returns focus to its trigger and successful restoration focuses the composer. Replies use a labelled log, busy state, feedback pressed states and live announcements. Touch actions remain visible; reduced motion disables message entrance and nonessential transitions.
chat-thread.demoBody: Replay restores the fixture. New chat shows the empty state. Send streams a local reply, Stop keeps the partial text, and messages sent during generation enter the existing queue. Edit and retry create versions; switching versions restores their own continuation. Error example exposes failure and retry. Load earlier messages, checkpoints and undo are interactive. Replies, model data, context compaction and file restoration are simulated; the demo does not contact a model, modify disk files or upload attachments. Response timings are measured from the local simulation; seed metrics and token counts are mock data. Changing the model selector affects future replies only.
chat-thread.compatibilityBody: The chat-thread-01 block retains every component, type, label set, history helper and demo-data export. Its old modules forward to this shared implementation and the same context. ToolCallsThread, SubagentsThread and ChatWorkspace now depend directly on the AI component. The standalone UI includes no demo fixtures or input composer dependency; install InputMessage separately if needed.
chat-thread.boundaryBody: ChatThread coordinates one conversation scroller, history anchors, message navigation, checkpoint requests and a persistent composer. Use ChatUserMessage and ChatAssistantMessage inside it: they register stable unique message IDs and reuse ChatMessage for presentation. A bare ChatMessage does not register a thread entry and cannot replace these wrappers directly. The host owns messages, versions, model requests and persistence.
chat-thread.aliasesBody: The names below remain exported from chat-thread and chat-thread-01, with @deprecated source hints pointing to recommended imports. New compositions use the corresponding chat-message primitives; thread entries still use ChatUserMessage / ChatAssistantMessage. ChatAction is a direct alias; the other component adapters require thread context. Preserve labels and disabled state when replacing them. ChatMarkdown, ChatCheckpoint, ChatDivider and the registered message wrappers remain supported conversation APIs.
chat-thread.aliasAction: Direct compatibility alias for ChatMessageAction; no thread context required.
chat-thread.aliasCopy: The adapter inherits thread labels. Pass copy, copied and copyFailed labels explicitly in new compositions.
chat-thread.aliasBranch: The adapter inherits thread labels and forwards disabled. Preserve labels, branch and disabled in new compositions.
chat-thread.aliasAttachments: The adapter uses the thread conversation label as its accessible label. Pass the same label explicitly.
chat-thread.aliasEditor: The adapter inherits thread labels and disables editing/saving while busy or pending. Preserve labels and disabled state; cancellation remains available.
chat-thread.aliasTypes: Retained aliases of the corresponding ChatMessage types. Existing assignments and parameter types stay compatible.
